Will DeviceSide work with your device? The table above answers per feature and integration, and DeviceSide's
Configure > Settings shows it per device once installed. This page has the detail: each tested device, each class of
device by integration, and what can't be done. Every mark links its proof.

## Levels of proof

Claims follow evidence, per class of device: devices that get the same command and run the same family of firmware,
such as Hue bulbs on Zigbee2MQTT. A test on one class says nothing about another, because makers' firmware answers the
same command differently ([the rules](evidence.md#levels)).

- 🟢 **Verified:** a maintainer tested it on a real device, or signed off on users' working reports of it. ✔ marks a
  run on the automated rig, "by hand" a maintainer's own test, and "by report" users' reports, each linking its issue.
- 🟡 **Documented:** no device of the class has been tested, but it gets the same call as a Verified device of the
  same maker's firmware, certification tests the same read on every device of the class, or other users already send
  the same call to every device of the class with no reported failure.
- ⚪ **Labs:** built, but not yet shown to work (no device has passed it and no rule above covers it), or held back
  by a maintainer to soak. It stays off until you turn on **Labs** in **Configure > Settings**, and may be withdrawn if
  it fails and isn't fixed ([the Labs flag](evidence.md#the-labs-flag)).
- 🔴 **Not supported:** no known command works on it, or it isn't built yet. DeviceSide refuses it rather than leave
  the device doing something you didn't ask for. Where it isn't built yet, a contributor's pull request can build it
  ([how to help](../CONTRIBUTING.md#how-to-help)).

**⚠️ Unmaintained** marks a feature no one is fixing: it still works as it did, but a bug in it stays unfixed until
someone fixes it or takes over the integration. **🔧 Untested fix** marks a feature changed in a release before anyone
could test it on a device ([caveats](evidence.md#caveats)).

DeviceSide is run by volunteers. If your device isn't here, or a feature doesn't work, please tell us with **Integrations > DeviceSide > Configure > Report a
device test result or bug**, or [open a report](https://github.com/DeviceSide/DeviceSide/issues/new?template=device_report.yml).
It goes to the maintainers of the integration you choose, and works or not, it helps: a working report helps ship a
Labs feature to everyone, and a "doesn't work" one goes to the people who decide whether to fix it, find it a
maintainer, or turn it off.

## Not supported

| Devices | Integrations | Features | Why | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Aqara lights | Zigbee2MQTT | turn on with timer | Its bulb ignored a timed on from off and stayed off | [source](https://github.com/DeviceSide/DeviceSide/blob/main/docs/integrations/zigbee2mqtt/research/aqara/2026-11-25-agl003-probe.md) |
| devices behind a Matter bridge | Matter | turn on with timer | A bridge's software answers the timer for its devices, which nothing found says it runs, so it could stay on, and DeviceSide's own off isn't built | [source](https://github.com/DeviceSide/DeviceSide/blob/main/docs/integrations/matter/internals.md#what-decides-the-call) |
| Hue smart plugs | Zigbee2MQTT, ZHA | turn on with timer | Most plugs and switches ignore the timer or read it as a delayed toggle, so it could stay on, and the calls that would serve them, DeviceSide's own off or the plug's auto-off, aren't built | [source](https://github.com/DeviceSide/DeviceSide/blob/main/docs/integrations/zigbee2mqtt/research/2026-11-14-timed-on-call-patterns.md) |
| <a id="hue-smart-scenes"></a>Hue smart scenes | Hue | set scene | A smart (All-Day) scene changes with the time of day, so it has no fixed settings to write | [source](https://github.com/DeviceSide/DeviceSide/blob/main/docs/integrations/hue/index.md#hue-smart-scenes) |
| IKEA LED2005R5 and LED2106R3 (TRÅDFRI GU10 white spectrum) | Zigbee2MQTT, ZHA | turn on with timer | It is reported to turn on with the timer and never turn off, and DeviceSide's own off, which would serve it, isn't built | [source](https://github.com/Koenkk/zigbee2mqtt/issues/29158) |
| IKEA outlets | Zigbee2MQTT, ZHA | turn on with timer | Most plugs and switches ignore the timer or read it as a delayed toggle, so it could stay on, and the calls that would serve them, DeviceSide's own off or the plug's auto-off, aren't built | [source](https://github.com/DeviceSide/DeviceSide/blob/main/docs/integrations/zigbee2mqtt/research/2026-11-14-timed-on-call-patterns.md) |
| <a id="lights-whose-driver-cant-stop-a-ramp"></a>lights whose driver can't stop a ramp | Control4 | smooth dimming | The light's driver says it can't stop a ramp, so a raise or lower couldn't be halted | [source](https://github.com/DeviceSide/DeviceSide/blob/main/docs/integrations/control4/index.md#lights-whose-driver-cant-stop-a-ramp) |
| <a id="lights-whose-driver-cant-stop-a-ramp-1"></a>lights whose driver can't stop a ramp | Control4 | stop | The light's driver says it can't stop a ramp, and it ignores the stop | [source](https://github.com/DeviceSide/DeviceSide/blob/main/docs/integrations/control4/index.md#lights-whose-driver-cant-stop-a-ramp) |
| multi-endpoint Matter devices | Matter | turn on with timer | Certification tests the timer on one endpoint, and nothing found says it tests the others, so one could stay on, and DeviceSide's own off isn't built | [source](https://github.com/DeviceSide/DeviceSide/blob/main/docs/integrations/matter/internals.md#what-decides-the-call) |
| other brands | Zigbee2MQTT, ZHA | turn on with timer | Too few reports say its brand runs the timer, and some lights and most plugs turn on and never off, so it could stay on; DeviceSide's own off, which would serve it, isn't built | [source](https://github.com/DeviceSide/DeviceSide/blob/main/docs/integrations/zigbee2mqtt/research/2026-11-14-timed-on-call-patterns.md) |
| other brands' standard lights | Zigbee2MQTT | turn on with timer | Too few reports say its brand runs the timer, and some lights and most plugs turn on and never off, so it could stay on; DeviceSide's own off, which would serve it, isn't built | [source](https://github.com/DeviceSide/DeviceSide/blob/main/docs/integrations/zigbee2mqtt/research/2026-11-14-timed-on-call-patterns.md) |
| other Tuya datapoint devices | Zigbee2MQTT | turn on with timer | Zigbee2MQTT would turn it on with no timer, so it would stay on | [source](https://github.com/DeviceSide/DeviceSide/blob/main/docs/integrations/zigbee2mqtt/research/2026-11-14-timed-on-call-patterns.md) |
| other Tuya devices | Zigbee2MQTT | turn on with timer | Zigbee2MQTT would turn it on with no timer, so it would stay on | [source](https://github.com/DeviceSide/DeviceSide/blob/main/docs/integrations/zigbee2mqtt/research/2026-11-14-timed-on-call-patterns.md) |
| other Tuya devices | ZHA | turn on with timer | ZHA's timer can turn it on or off long after the time asked | [source](https://github.com/DeviceSide/DeviceSide/blob/main/docs/integrations/zigbee2mqtt/research/2026-11-14-timed-on-call-patterns.md) |
| Sengled bulbs | ZHA | turn on with timer | It refuses the timer, so with brightness, a color temperature or in a group it would stay on | [source](https://github.com/DeviceSide/DeviceSide/blob/main/docs/integrations/zha/internals.md#tested-behavior) |
| Sonoff S60ZBTPF and S60ZBTPG | Zigbee2MQTT | auto-off/on | Its inching can't be turned off: Zigbee2MQTT's DISABLE is reported to have no effect on it, so it would keep turning itself off | [source](https://github.com/DeviceSide/DeviceSide/blob/main/docs/integrations/zigbee2mqtt/research/sonoff/2026-11-24-inching.md) |
| Sonoff S60ZBTPF and S60ZBTPG | Zigbee2MQTT | turn on with timer | Too few reports say its brand runs the timer, and some lights and most plugs turn on and never off, so it could stay on; DeviceSide's own off, which would serve it, isn't built | [source](https://github.com/DeviceSide/DeviceSide/blob/main/docs/integrations/zigbee2mqtt/research/2026-11-14-timed-on-call-patterns.md) |

| Sonoff SWV | ZHA | turn on with timer | It reads ZHA's timer in seconds, so it would stay open about ten times longer than asked | [source](https://github.com/DeviceSide/DeviceSide/blob/main/docs/integrations/zigbee2mqtt/research/2026-11-14-tuya-countdown.md) |
| Tuya countdown plugs and switches (TS011F, TS0001–TS0004, TS0011, TS0726) | ZHA | turn on with timer | ZHA's timer can turn it on long after the time asked and leave it on | [source](https://github.com/DeviceSide/DeviceSide/blob/main/docs/integrations/zigbee2mqtt/research/2026-11-14-lab-probe.md) |

| Tuya WHD02 (_TZ3000_skueekg3, model TS0001) and Mowe MW781Z (_TZ300A_rncj86af) | Zigbee2MQTT | turn on with timer | Zigbee2MQTT would turn it on with no timer, so it would stay on | [source](https://github.com/DeviceSide/DeviceSide/blob/main/docs/integrations/zigbee2mqtt/research/2026-11-14-timed-on-call-patterns.md) |
